A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaudio–Joshi work on spectral algorithms for exact community recovery. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results, algorithms, proofs, and analytic threshold diagrams, but no experimental or simulation outcomes. The acknowledgement of simulation work does not report results.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation success rates for Z2-synchronization and symmetric SBM in Figures 2, 4, and 5, using n=300 and 50 trials.

M1.justification: v1 handles BEC side information through label overrides and BSC information through weighted shifts. v2 Algorithms 2, 5, and 6 accept general node attributes and add their log-likelihood ratios, including a new Gaussian-feature rule. This substantially broadens supported inputs while retaining the eigenvector construction and BEC/BSC degree-profiling procedures.

E1.justification: v2 introduces empirical evaluation where v1 had only theoretical coverage: synthetic Z2-synchronization with Gaussian-feature, BEC, and BSC side information, and symmetric SBM with BEC and BSC side information. These are actual simulations reported in Figure 2 and Appendix A.1.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparisons against competing algorithms. v2 evaluates its spectral algorithm; the curves labelled with and without side information are theoretical thresholds, not evaluated comparator methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds a simulation protocol using n=300 and exact-recovery success rates. Z2-synchronization sweeps signal and side-information strength; symmetric SBM sweeps a and b at beta=0.5 and 0.7. Appendix A.1 specifies Gaussian-feature and channel parameterizations. v1 contains no corresponding evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The new fixed-size parameter sweeps examine how recovery success changes with edge signal and side-information strength, including the two SBM beta settings. This adds limited empirical sensitivity evidence to v1's analytic phase diagrams; no separate component ablations or error analyses are introduced.

E5.justification: v2 reports 50 trials for the simulation grids, explicitly independent for the SBM experiments, and displays success frequencies. v1 has no empirical repeated-run reporting. Confidence intervals, seed specifications, and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: Figures 2, 4, and 5 add numerical success-rate heatmaps absent from v1. They show finite-size recovery transitions as signal and side-information strength vary, including expanded successful SBM regions with stronger side information. These are newly reported outcomes, with no corresponding v1 measurements for a performance comparison.

T1.justification: v2 replaces much of v1's case-specific threshold and impossibility analysis with a Renyi-divergence formulation, Proposition 2.10 adapted from Dreveton et al., and a general genie-margin proof. It adds Gaussian-feature derivations and broadens the SBM theorem's stated parameter domain. Its new BSC threshold expression is also not equivalent to v1's piecewise ROS threshold.

C1.justification: v1 claims both derivation of information-theoretic limits and optimal algorithms for BEC/BSC settings. v2 credits the general limits to Dreveton et al. and centers its contribution on efficient spectral achievability for general node-attributed side information, including Gaussian features. The abstract and contribution statements therefore change substantially in scope and attribution.

C2.justification: Remark A.1 newly discusses unknown parameters, the uncertain practical advantage over two-stage methods when preliminary estimation is required, and unresolved BSC plug-in accuracy. Appendix A.2 develops applicability conditions for broader distribution families and multiple communities, including eigenvalue-degeneracy obstacles and a hypergraph example explaining spectral suboptimality.

D1.justification: Remark 5.3 adds implementation guidance through sequential eigenpair computation, nearly linear input-size runtime, and O(n) side-information processing. Appendix A.1 documents the new simulation-generation parameters, while Remark A.1 adds parameter-estimation guidance. These are limited additions to the existing detailed pseudocode.

R1.justification: Dreveton et al. (2024) becomes a central foundation for the threshold results and changes the paper's positioning toward algorithmic achievability. v2 also expands discussion of local-to-global methods, spatial and labelled models, and hypergraph spectral limitations, rather than merely updating citation formatting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. v2 separates genie estimation from algorithm construction, expands the spectral explanation, moves degree-profiling theorem statements into the appendices, and reorganizes related work and deferred discussions. These changes extend beyond the presentation of newly added science.

P2.justification: v2 adds three multi-panel simulation figures and a main-text algorithm sketch, and removes the two explicit threshold-table displays. v1 Figure 2 is retained as v2 Figure 6, while the side-information illustration is relocated and the proof-framework diagram retained. The visual presentation changes substantially.

improvement.justification: Broader side-information support, simulations, and practical limitations improve scope and usefulness. However, v2 Appendix A.1 implies ROS BSC I*=Psi/8+beta/2, conflicting with its retained Figure 6 and v1 Table 1. At Psi=4 and beta=0.9, the formulas give 0.95 versus 1.05125, placing recovery on opposite sides of the threshold. This unresolved inconsistency affects the central optimality claim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
